findings.title: The E002 result behind A2–A5 and K1–K3 is not in the repository at this commit
findings.detail: EV-O001-01 relies on E002-20261016T054426-b69a for four of the six pass criteria and all three kill criteria. That run does not exist in this snapshot: experiments/results/ holds only E000, E001 and E003. The evaluation file is also missing; project/objectives/O001/ has no evaluations/ directory. Without the result I cannot check its git_dirty flag or spec_hash. I cannot check whether the gating sanity checks passed: all_drc_valid, l2_extrapolation_verified, l2_converged, l2_solver_ok, sample_diverse. I cannot recompute rho = 0.9959, MAPE = 0.0972 or recall = 1.0, or reproduce the PASS verdict. The evaluator (evaluate.select_results) checks neither that results are committed nor the runner hash recorded at run time, so its own validity_problems = [] does not establish provenance.

Grepping project, experiments, research, docs and .mfos for 'b69a' finds it only in the review packet. findings.title: The pooled ranking metrics cannot tell layout-level ranking apart from sorting by topology and die count
findings.detail: Within the claimed scope, L is dominated by family and die count, both of which are fixed inputs, not the design choices a re-layout search ranks. I tested this on the pre-registered design pool. A predictor that knows only each layout's (family, dies) stratum mean, with zero within-stratum information, scores: pooled Spearman 0.967 (minimum 0.944 over 2000 stratified 90-layout draws), above A3 (0.90) and A2 (0.85); top-decile recall ≥ 0.70 in 99.3% of draws (A5), with recall = 1.0 in 51%; MAPE 5.5% (under A4); and within-family Spearman 0.85. So A2, A3 and A5, and even the secondary spearman_rho_within_family (which pools dies 2–6), would pass for a model that cannot rank two layouts with the same family and die count. The product use is derivative re-layouts at a fixed die count inside a fixed housing, which is a within-stratum decision. The observed 0.9959 fits roughly 2% independent per-layout error, which would mean within-stratum rho ≈ 0.89 (simulated), but that is inferred, not measured. E002's MAPE (9.7%) is larger than the within-stratum spread of L (CV 5–10%), so within-stratum ordering depends entirely on the L1 error being common-mode within each stratum. Nothing in the material shows that.
findings.evidence: research/e002_design/pool_l1.json: 1500 L1 values, 100 per stratum. 97.3% of log-L variance lies between (family, dies) strata, 2.7% within. Within-stratum CV of L: interleaved 5.7–6.1%, u_shaped 4.8–5.9%, side_by_side 7.2–10.4%. Noise simulation (6 layouts per stratum, 200 reps): independent multiplicative error sd 1/2/3% → pooled rho 0.9987/0.9962/0.9927, mean within-stratum rho 0.95/0.89/0.82.
findings.suggested_check: From the existing E002 L1/L2_inf rows (no new solves), report Spearman and top-k recall within each (family, dies) stratum and stratum-demeaned, and compare them with the stratum-only baseline.

findings.title: A1 validates a different L2 code path from the one used as the E002 reference
findings.detail: A1 (max relative error 1.3e-4 against closed forms) is E001's metric for moduleforge.solvers.l2 on canonical bars, round-wire chains and a wire loop over an image plane. E002's reference is moduleforge.solvers.l2_layout (TOOL_VERSION 0.3.0). That is a separate path: top-Cu, backside-Cu and baseplate slabs on a shared lattice, a precorrected-FFT wire-to-grid operator, bilinear point contacts and die-short node merges, with its own change history (T0075 attempts 1–5). Its only analytic anchor in the material is the in-run C1 check: one Al wire loop over one plane slab, within 2% of the closed form and 0.5% of l2. No closed-form or independent check covers the top-Cu trace-over-plane slab inductance, which dominates these loops, or the contact and die-short treatment. E002 checks L2's convergence by Richardson extrapolation, but convergence is not correctness. A1 therefore does not support 'converged reference solver' for the solver actually used.
findings.evidence: src/moduleforge/solvers/l2_layout.py docstring; E001 spec cases A1–C1 run through solvers.l2 (E001 result provenance 6cc5821, 2026-10-06); E002 sanity check l2_layout_reference_valid covers C1 only.
findings.suggested_check: Run l2_layout on E001's bar and strip cases (B-series), or on a straight strip over a ground plane against Wheeler or 2-D BEM values, with the cell sizes E002 used.

findings.title: The claim covers AMB substrates, but no AMB layout was tested
findings.detail: The claim and scope_in name 'single DBC or AMB substrate'. generate.halfbridge._build always uses default_dbc_stack(): Al2O3, 0.38 mm ceramic, 0.3 mm Cu. default_amb_stack() (0.32 mm Si3N4) is never used by E002 or E003. One substrate outline (70×40 mm) and one fixed pad placement are used throughout. L1's main stated bias, unresolved HF edge-current crowding, scales with the Cu-to-plane gap, and the L1 docstring reports it as family-dependent. So agreement on one DBC stack does not carry over to AMB without a test.
findings.evidence: src/moduleforge/generate/halfbridge.py line 109: `stack = default_dbc_stack()`. src/moduleforge/geometry/stack.py defines default_amb_stack (0.32 mm), which the generator never calls.
findings.suggested_check: Narrow the claim to the tested Al2O3 DBC stack, or run a small sealed E002-style comparison on default_amb_stack.

findings.title: A2 and A4 bounds exclude the reference-extrapolation uncertainty that the E002 design names as the reference-robust reading
findings.detail: The design note (research/notes/o001-e002-e003-design.md §3.3) states: 'A2 iff spearman refband_lo ≥ 0.85; A4 iff mape refband_hi ≤ 0.12'. The spec's metric descriptions say the same. The evaluation instead reads the bootstrap CI of spearman_rho_Lloop and mape_Lloop, which covers sampling over layouts only, not the common-ratio Richardson band of L2_inf. A4's margin is 0.102 against 0.12. A band of about ±1% on L2_inf (the l2_converged limit) shifts MAPE by a similar amount, so A4 probably still holds. However, mape_Lloop_refband_hi cannot be checked because the result is missing.
findings.evidence: Evaluation A4 bound_used 0.10200817; objective A4 uses E002.mape_Lloop with uncertainty use: ci.
findings.suggested_check: Read mape_Lloop_refband_hi and spearman_rho_Lloop_refband_lo from the E002 result and confirm both clear their thresholds.

findings.title: No recorded link shows the timed L1 is the same code as the ranked L1
findings.detail: E003 ran at commit 4c8cf3e on 2026-10-12, four days before E002 was registered (2026-10-16). E003's result records no source hash for physics/peec, and neither commit is resolvable in this snapshot. If L1 changed between the runs, A6 timed a different model. The margin is large (p50 22.4 ms against 50 ms; the 6-die stratum p50 is 26.3 ms), and the L1 docstring's 'p50 ~25 ms on the 6-die benchmark' is consistent with it. The measurement was on an Apple M5 under macOS with no core pinning, which is conservative.
findings.suggested_check: Record the sha256 of src/moduleforge/physics/peec/*.py in both the E002 and E003 results, or re-time at the E002 commit.

findings.title: Points in favour of the claim
findings.detail: L2 is physically independent of L1's key approximation: l2_layout meshes the backside Cu and baseplate as conducting slabs and uses no image planes. My hand calculation gives Cu skin depth δ = 14.8 µm at 20 MHz, so t/δ ≈ 20 for the 0.3 mm backside Cu. A single image plane at its top face is justified, with field transmission through it ≈ 1.5e-9. The neglected plane recession (~δ/2 against the 0.38 mm gap, about 2%) is common-mode. E001 and E003 results are complete, report git_dirty = false and spec hashes matching the registered specs, and every declared sanity check passed. Their metric values equal the A1 and A6 values in the evaluation.

independent_checks_performed: Recomputed the sha256 of experiments/runners/e001_reference.py, e002_ranking.py and e003_timing.py: all three match the registered runner_files hashes.
Recomputed spec_hash for E001, E002 and E003 with mfos Store.spec_hash: all match. Recomputed the O001 criteria_hash: sha256:d12d7746…, equal to the evaluation's.
Searched the repository for the E002 run ID and for any E002 result artifact: none exists. Only E000, E001 and E003 results are present, and the EV-O001-01 file is also absent.
Read the E001 and E003 result.json files: status complete, git_dirty false, spec hashes match, every sanity check passed. A1 = 1.329e-4 and A6 = 22.39 ms reproduce from the files.

Stratum-only baseline on research/e002_design/pool_l1.json (1500 L1 values): pooled Spearman 0.967 (minimum 0.944 over 2000 stratified 90-layout draws); top-decile recall ≥ 0.7 in 99.3% of draws; MAPE 0.055; within-family Spearman 0.85; 97.3% of log-L variance lies between strata.
Noise simulation mapping pooled rho to within-stratum rho (independent multiplicative error of 0.5–4%): the observed 0.9959 corresponds to about 2% error and within-stratum rho ≈ 0.89.
Read the generator: only default_dbc_stack() is used, so no AMB layouts were tested.

Read the L1 model (physics/peec/model.py, kernels.py) and the L2 layout solver documentation: L2 meshes the planes as slabs and uses no images, so it is independent of L1's image-plane approximation. Hand calculation: skin depth at 20 MHz = 14.8 µm, t/δ ≈ 20, so imaging only the backside Cu is justified.
Read mfos evaluate.py: the evaluator does not check that results are committed or the runner hash recorded at run time, and A2/A4 use the bootstrap CI rather than the refband readings.
caveats: What is missing: the E002 result directory experiments/results/E002/E002-20261016T054426-b69a (result.json, run.json, per-layout L1/L2 rows) and project/objectives/O001/evaluations/EV-O001-01.json. Without them, A2–A5, K1–K3 and every E002 sanity check are unverifiable.

Running product code (L1 timing, L1 or L2 solves) was denied in this environment. I did not independently re-time L1 or re-solve any layout. The stratum-baseline analysis uses the pre-registered L1 design pool as a stand-in for the L2 distribution.
The snapshot contains one commit, so I could not check that the result commits (6cc5821, 4c8cf3e) are on main, or whether L1 changed between E003 and E002.

Even with the E002 artifact supplied and clean, the best obtainable verdict would be accept_with_caveats. The evidence supports pooled ranking across families and die counts on one Al2O3 DBC stack and one housing. It does not show ranking within a fixed family and die count, and it does not cover AMB substrates.
